items.title: Adam Smith warned against corporate collusion
items.claim: Adam Smith is often invoked as a free-market champion. What did he actually say about businessmen meeting together?

options.text: That free assembly among capitalists is the engine of innovation
That 'People of the same trade seldom meet together... but the conversation ends in a conspiracy against the public, or in some contrivance to raise prices.'
That competition is a myth used by economists
Nothing — he never discussed business behaviour

items.reveal:
The quote is from The Wealth of Nations (1776), Book I, Chapter X. Smith was deeply suspicious of merchant power and joint-stock companies. He criticised the East India Company at length and warned that 'the proposal of any new law or regulation of commerce which comes from this order ought always to be listened to with great precaution.'

The 'invisible hand' appears only three times in his works, with a meaning closer to 'unintended consequences of self-interested behaviour, when channelled by competition' than 'markets always good'.
items.why: Smith is invoked rhetorically by people who haven't read him. The actual Wealth of Nations is alert to monopoly, collusion and the political power of capital — closer to a regulatory liberal than a libertarian.

items.title: Japan's debt-to-GDP is over 250% — and it hasn't defaulted
items.claim: Japan's general government gross debt was around 263% of GDP in 2023 (IMF). What's the orthodox explanation for why this hasn't triggered a sovereign debt crisis?

options.text: Japan does not actually have debt

Debt is mostly held domestically (BOJ, pension funds, banks) in yen, with the BOJ controlling the curve; net debt is lower; current account surplus; large household savings. Foreign-currency emerging market debt is structurally different

items.reveal_title: Composition matters as much as level
items.reveal:
Reinhart and Rogoff's controversial 2010 'Growth in a Time of Debt' suggested debt above 90% of GDP harmed growth. Subsequent re-analysis (Herndon, Ash, Pollin 2013) found an Excel error and weaker results. The relationship between debt levels and outcomes depends heavily on currency denomination, holders, monetary regime and growth rates.

Greece (2010-12) and Sri Lanka (2022) had foreign-currency exposure that Japan lacks. The UK has a Liability Driven Investment (LDI) crisis in autumn 2022 despite much lower debt levels — composition and confidence matter.
items.why: Headline debt-to-GDP misleads about sustainability. Currency, holders, maturity profile, monetary regime and growth trajectory matter as much as the ratio itself.

items.title: The middle income trap is real but not universal
items.claim: Many countries that reached middle income status (typically $4,000-$12,000 GDP per capita) have struggled to advance to high income. Which describes the phenomenon best?

options.text: A subset (Brazil, South Africa, Argentina, Thailand) have plateaued; others (South Korea, Singapore, Taiwan, more recently Poland) have transitioned successfully. Drivers include education, institutional quality, R&D, and shifting from labour-intensive to knowledge-intensive production
All countries reach high income automatically

items.reveal:
The term was popularised by Indermit Gill and Homi Kharas's 2007 World Bank study. World Bank research (2013, 2018) found about 13 of 101 middle-income economies in 1960 reached high income by 2008.

South Korea's transition from low- to high-income was unusually rapid (1960-2000). It combined export orientation, investment in education and selective industrial policy. Argentina's reversal (from rich to middle income across the 20th century) shows the direction isn't fixed.
items.why: Development outcomes are heterogeneous. Single-factor explanations (geography, institutions, culture) often capture parts of the story but don't generalise.
